key_insight: CS3F shows that frozen 2D foundation models can be repurposed, without training, to detect and localize anomalies in 3D medical volumes by comparing local tokens across subjects.
clinical_relevance: This could help flag suspicious regions in MRI or CT when labeled 3D training data are scarce or when imaging protocols and patient populations vary.
method: Decompose each 3D scan along multiple axes and encode slices with a 2D vision transformer.
Pool neighboring slice features into localized volumetric tokens.
Score anomalies by cross-subject mutual similarity, then refine with coarse-to-fine tokenization for better focal lesion detection.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on brain MRI for metastases, glioma, and stroke, and also validated on lung CT to test generalizability beyond brain imaging.
watch_item: Fine tokenization may not help equally across modalities or low-contrast lesions, and depth pooling can still attenuate small focal abnormalities.
paper_title: Toward Training-Free Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection in 3D Medical Images: A Batch-Based Approach Using 2D Foundation Models
